name: Minutemen
label: SST
lede: Three guys from San Pedro, songs that ended before a radio DJ could find the volume knob, forty-five of them on one record, and a van on Interstate 10 that took it all away.

hero.by: Mike Watt, D. Boon and George Hurley, 1982. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: A boy falls out of a tree
eras.text: D. Boon and Mike Watt were San Pedro harbor-town kids who learned rock by copying records on pawnshop guitars. After a false start as the Reactionaries, they built a band with no frontman, no wasted seconds and no plan beyond playing, and Black Flag handed them a record deal.

years.h: D. Boon and Mike Watt form the Reactionaries
years.p: [[D. Boon|ae1757eb-8679-4cb3-8d3a-33160c953505]], [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]], drummer [[George Hurley|e3644b83-1c19-41fa-bf81-483551cd1588]] and singer Martin Tamburovich play as the Reactionaries in San Pedro. Boon and Watt later ditch the idea of a frontman as bourgeois.
years.xp:
The two had met as kids when D. Boon, playing army with other boys in a San Pedro park, fell out of a tree right next to Watt. Boon's mother taught him guitar and encouraged Watt to learn bass.

Their first instruments came from a pawnshop, one for $15 and one for $13.

years.h: Minutemen form, with a welder named Frank Tonche on drums
years.p: D. Boon and Mike Watt write their first songs, then play a couple of gigs with local welder Frank Tonche. The name mocks a 1960s right-wing militia group, not the song lengths.

years.cap: Opening for Black Flag, San Pedro
years.h: First gig: opening for Black Flag in San Pedro
years.p: Minutemen's first show is an opening slot for [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] in their hometown. [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]] likes them enough to offer a record on his new label, SST.

years.h: Frank Tonche quits; George Hurley takes the drums
years.p: Frank Tonche says he doesn't like the crowd the band is drawing. [[George Hurley|e3644b83-1c19-41fa-bf81-483551cd1588]], who'd drummed in the Reactionaries, joins for good.

years.h: Paranoid Time: SST 002, seven songs in 6 minutes 31
years.p: Cut in one late-night session at Media Art in Hermosa Beach on July 20, with no overdubs except backing vocals. [[Raymond Pettibon|3e603b97-d5f8-4547-891b-74cdfd2ed7bf]] draws the cover.
years.xp:
Mike Watt can be heard directing his bandmates before 'Joe McCarthy's Ghost', and George Hurley's brother Greg sings backup. Early covers were printed black, later ones green.

Greg Ginn walked Watt and D. Boon through how a record gets made, and they took notes: next came their own label, New Alliance.

eras.title: Jamming econo
eras.text: Minutemen worked like the dockworkers they grew up around: cheap sessions, songs under a minute, vans instead of hotels. Watt had a phrase for it, jamming econo, and it became a creed for American indie rock.

years.h: Joy EP comes out on Watt and Boon's own label
years.p: Mike Watt and D. Boon start New Alliance Records after learning the ropes from Greg Ginn. The Joy EP is New Alliance No. 3, with D. Boon's own cover art.

years.h: The Punch Line: 18 songs, done in about a quarter hour
years.p: The first Minutemen album, SST 004, is D. Boon's scratchy guitar, Mike Watt's lead bass and George Hurley's drums, mostly without a verse-chorus structure in sight. D. Boon drew the cover.

years.h: Bean-Spill EP on Thermidor, and a live set on KPFK radio
years.p: Minutemen release the Bean-Spill EP on Thermidor and play a live set on Los Angeles community station KPFK.

years.h: What Makes a Man Start Fires?, the second album
years.p: SST 014, the second Minutemen album, mixing hardcore speed with funk and jazz.

years.h: Buzz or Howl Under the Influence of Heat EP
years.p: SST 016 comes out the same month Minutemen start recording Double Nickels on the Dime at Radio Tokyo with Ethan James.

eras.title: Forty-five songs at 55 miles an hour
eras.text: When Hüsker Dü made a double album, Minutemen made a bigger one, for $1,100. Two years later they were opening for R.E.M., trying on a commercial sound, and planning a triple album. Then D. Boon was gone.

q: It wasn't really a competition even.
years.h: Hüsker Dü's Zen Arcade turns Double Nickels into a double
years.p: After hearing labelmates [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]] cut the double album Zen Arcade, Minutemen go back and write enough songs to make their own a double.
years.xp: Watt wrote 'Take that Hüskers!' on the record, but insists it was a thank-you: Hüsker Dü gave them the idea. Each member picked the songs for one side; the fourth side, the leftovers, is labeled 'Chaff'.

years.cap: Mike Watt at the wheel, 55 mph on I-10. Photo: Dirk Vandenberg
years.h: Double Nickels on the Dime: 45 songs for $1,100
years.p: Recorded at Radio Tokyo in Venice with Ethan James and mixed in one night on an eight-track. The title needles Sammy Hagar's 'I Can't Drive 55'.
years.xp:
Dirk Vandenberg shot the cover from the back seat as Mike Watt drove his Volkswagen Beetle at exactly 55 on Interstate 10 toward San Pedro. It took three highway loops and two days.

'History Lesson – Part II', 'Corona' and 'Jesus and Tequila' are here, plus covers of Creedence Clearwater Revival and Van Halen. Spin gave it 10 out of 10; Pitchfork put it at No. 17 of the 1980s.

years.h: History Lesson – Part II: the song that named a book
years.p: D. Boon and Mike Watt's history of their own band, on Double Nickels on the Dime. Michael Azerrad took its opening line for the title of Our Band Could Be Your Life in 2001.

years.h: Project: Mersh: Minutemen try going commercial
years.p: Six songs aimed at radio, the title Pedro slang for commercial. The underground hates it and it sells poorly next to Double Nickels on the Dime.

years.h: Minutemen and Black Flag record together as Minuteflag
years.p: The two SST bands cut a joint EP, Minuteflag. SST holds it until early 1986, after D. Boon's death.

years.h: Last show: Charlotte, North Carolina, opening for R.E.M.
years.p: Minutemen play their final concert in Charlotte on a run opening for [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] Nobody knows it's the last one.

years.h: 3-Way Tie (For Last): the last Minutemen album
years.p: SST 058 comes out in December 1985, the same month D. Boon dies. D. Boon drew the cover art.

years.h: D. Boon killed in a van crash on Interstate 10 in Arizona
years.p: Around 4:40 a.m., east of Quartzsite, the van's rear axle breaks. D. Boon, lying in the back with a fever and no seatbelt, is thrown out and dies of a broken neck. He was 27.
years.xp:
His girlfriend Linda Kite was driving. D. Boon had been born in San Pedro on April 1, 1958.

Watt has said he and D. Boon had just been talking about a triple album. Minutemen ended that morning; Watt and Hurley refused to go on under the name.

eras.title: Sonic Youth hands Watt a bass
eras.text: Mike Watt fell into a deep depression, and it took friends from New York to get him playing again. The band that remained became a ballot box for its fans, and a kid from Ohio was about to start calling.

q: Thurston asked me to play bass on Evol. That was a big highlight, man.
years.h: Thurston Moore asks Mike Watt to play on Sonic Youth's EVOL
years.p: [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] bring Mike Watt to New York and put him on bass on EVOL. The Ciccone Youth side project is dreamed up partly to get him making music.

years.h: Mike Watt and George Hurley start fIREHOSE with Ed Crawford
years.p: Ohio State student [[Ed Crawford|c02f03fe-93cf-4590-841b-1b9f04d6a694]] talks his way into a jam, and [[fIREHOSE|33e09dd8-a998-4e1a-9e69-1a6567a3803d]] is born. The lowercase f nods to the all-caps Minutemen logo.

years.h: Ballot Result: the fans pick the songs
years.p: Mike Watt and George Hurley mail out ballots and build a live double album from the votes, with recordings from 1980 to November 1985.

eras.title: Our band could be your life
eras.text: Two decades after the crash, Minutemen found a bigger audience than they ever had: a stunt show's theme song, a book named after one of their songs, and a documentary that premiered in the town that made them.

years.h: 'Corona' becomes the Jackass theme
years.p: The instrumental parts of D. Boon's 'Corona', from Double Nickels on the Dime, open MTV's Jackass, putting Minutemen on MTV.

years.h: Michael Azerrad's Our Band Could Be Your Life gives them a chapter
years.p: Azerrad's history of 1980s indie rock takes its title from a Minutemen song and says they proved regular Joes could make great art.

years.h: Mike Watt and George Hurley play Minutemen songs as a duo
years.p: On rare nights, mostly around Los Angeles, the two play a set of Minutemen songs for bass and drums only. No one fills in for D. Boon, and they won't bill it as Minutemen.

years.h: We Jam Econo premieres at the Warner Grand in San Pedro
years.p: Tim Irwin's documentary We Jam Econo: The Story of the Minutemen premieres in the band's hometown theater. The DVD follows in June 2006.
